column1: # Events for mods (dev.xavier.stein.bridge.hooks.GameHooks, which hand them to the Stein Loader), at the points where Forge 1.8.9
# fires the equivalents. With no mod on the classpath, each hook checks an empty list
# Minecraft.run (a): startGame (am) — before (resource packs) and after (FMLInitializationEvent).
# runGameLoop (av): after each runTick (s) — ClientTickEvent END.
# Keyboard and mouse loops of runTick: each iteration's next() announces the previous event.
# New renderer (step 6): HUD and screens recorded. The end of the HUD session comes AFTER the mods' overlay (same key,
# the order of the rules is the order of the hooks), so the mods' HUD is recorded too.
# A hidden HUD (GameHooks.hideHud, the Loader's Hud.setHidden: the replay) skips the whole renderGameOverlay.
# GuiScreen.handleInput (p): each mouse event of an open screen.
# NetHandlerPlayClient.handleChat (bcy.a(Lfy;)V): chat message before the chat.
# S01PacketJoinGame.processPacket: server join completed, on the game thread.
# effect list from the inventory (the screen stops shifting sideways).
# GuiMainMenu.drawScreen (aya.a(IIF)V): the "Minecraft 1.8.9" line becomes the version block
# in the bottom-left corner (game, SteinBridge, Loader), like Forge's.
# GuiScreen.mouseClicked (axu.a(III)V): a button click goes through the mods before the
# EntityRenderer.getFOVModifier (bfk.a(FZ)F, private; 6 calls inside EntityRenderer itself):
# the frame's field of view goes through the mods (Forge's EntityViewRenderEvent.FOVModifier).
# EntityRenderer.updateFovModifierHand (bfk.l): the player's FOV factor (speed, bow)
# goes through the mods before smoothing (Forge's FOVUpdateEvent).
# TextureMap (bmh): before the atlas is built (loadTextureAtlas, in loadSprites), mods register
# textures (Forge's TextureStitchEvent.Pre); when stitching, a texture with a path under mcpatcher/ or
# optifine/ is read from assets/<domain>/<path>.png, the way resource packs lay out custom item textures (CIT).
# ModelManager.onResourceManagerReload (bou.a): after reloadModels, models and atlas are ready.
# ItemModelMesher.getItemModel (bfo.a): the model of each drawn item goes through the mods.
# A slot on each ItemStack for mods to keep what they computed about it (Game.itemData).
# LayerArmorBase.renderLayer (bkn.a(Lpr;FFFFFFFI)V): the piece (getCurrentArmor) and its texture
# (getArmorResource, with and without overlay) go through the mods (ForgeHooksClient.getArmorTexture).
# GuiOverlayDebug.renderDebugInfoRight (avv.b): SteinBridge and Loader lines in F3.
# Visual options (engine/Visuals, via the Loader API). RenderManager.doRenderEntity (biu.a):
# the Render receives the entity's position relative to the camera — distance for glow and nametags.
# HUD grid (Stein Loader, API 9; hooks/VanillaHud): parts of the game's own HUD that the Loader takes over to move,
# reshape or turn off — the action bar (the body of GuiIngame.setRecordPlaying: the IChatComponent one; the record one and
# mods go through it), the boss bar (renderBossHealth in renderGameOverlay) and the sidebar scoreboard (renderScoreboard).
# ... and the dark box behind the chat lines ("Background" option): the three Gui.drawRect calls inside

# GuiNewChat.drawChat go through the Bridge (the owner at the call site is GuiNewChat itself, which inherits drawRect from Gui), which skips the line's one (alpha only) and keeps the two of the scroll bar (with color).
# API 8: the click's hit (PlayerControllerMP.attackEntity in Minecraft.clickMouse) goes through the mods,
# which can cancel it (allies); the name in the Tab list (GuiPlayerTabOverlay.getPlayerName in renderPlayerlist) and the name above
# the head (getDisplayName in RendererLivingEntity.renderName) too; and, before the super.onLivingUpdate of
# EntityPlayerSP (which moves the player), sprinting in all directions (engine/Sprint).
# API 0.1.15 (Inventory, Targeting): the entity interaction of rightClickMouse (both calls), which mods can
# cancel; every PlayerControllerMP.windowClick in the game (no scope: it is the path of every slot click), which mods
# see and can cancel; and, in handleSetSlot (S2F) and handleWindowItems (S30), the slot or window already applied.
# API 0.1.15 (damage): in handleEntityStatus (S19) the entity status goes through the mods (2 = damage, which they can remove
# from the client; 3 = death); in handleEntityMetadata (S1C) and handleUpdateHealth (S06), health and absorption before and
# after, for whoever displays the damage.
# ... and the miss penalty (API 14): missing a click sets ten ticks (half a second) during which clickMouse returns at the
# first line, so aiming at someone in the middle of an autoclick does not hit. The condition that sets it (isNotCreative) goes
# through the Bridge, which answers as creative when the mod turns the penalty off; only inside clickMouse.
# RendererLivingEntity.renderName (bjl.b): nametag up to the chosen distance. Only this call site: the
# other is RenderLiving's super.canRenderName (bjo, invokespecial), and if it were redirected the virtual dispatch
# would come back to bjo in recursion.
# MathHelper.sin/cos (ns.a, ns.b) in drawing code only: model animations (client/model), particles, entity, layer and
# tile entity renderers, the view bobbing and camera of EntityRenderer and the hand and item of ItemRenderer go through
# AngleTable (the game's table, or the compact one with the "compact angles" option). Movement, physics and every
# other piece of game logic keep calling the game's own MathHelper untouched, so the option never changes where a
# player steps. One rule per calling method (the call sites were listed from the game jar by class package).
# EntityRenderer.setupFog (bfk.a(IF)V): start and end recorded (setFogStart/End, bfl.b/c) and, after
# enableFog (bfl.m), the terrain fog from the option. getRenderViewEntity (ave.ac) is the first call.
# RenderGlobal.renderClouds / renderCloudsFancy (bfr.b(FI)V, bfr.c(FI)V): cloud height from the option.
# The camera's roll on taking damage (Visuals.hurtRotate): the GlStateManager.rotate calls inside
# EntityRenderer.hurtCameraEffect, scoped, so they win over the matrix stack's unscoped rule.
# The resource packs' sky (sky.CustomSky): in RenderGlobal.renderSky, the bind of the sun's texture draws the packs'
# sky layers first (the other binds there pass through).
# Direct drawing (engine/DirectRender): the isFramebufferEnabled that Framebuffer, ScreenShotHelper and
# LoadingScreenRenderer query; post-processing shaders and spectator outline (they need
# the framebuffer); F2 deferred to before the buffer swap (dispatchKeypresses, ave.Z).
# Chunk building pace (engine/ChunkPace, options): submissions per frame and waiting for neighbors in
# updateChunks (bfr.a(J)V); those adjacent to the player go through ChunkSync.buildNear.
# Model of each block built into the chunk (BlockRendererDispatcher.renderBlock -> BlockModelRenderer.renderModel,
# on the building threads): only the blocks marked by a mod (the Block's sbModelHook field, Game.watchBlockModel)
# go through it — Stein Lens's connected blocks; the others only pay for reading the field.
# Extended distance (engine/ChunkKeep, option): the doPreChunk of the chunk handlers (S21 and S26) — a server
# discard becomes a stored column; before each Minecraft.loadWorld (join, respawn, leave), the disk saves the
# world that is going away. The frame() comes from ChunkPace.uploads.
# No rain (engine/Rain, "Rain" option off): WorldClient.getRainStrength returns 0 for the three places in the
# client that draw rain — renderRainSnow (drop and flake), addRainParticles (splash and sound) and renderSky (overcast
# sky). The server and the rest of the game keep the real rain (World.getRainStrength does not change).
# Tab list (Stein HUD draws its own): in place of GuiPlayerTabOverlay.renderPlayerlist inside
# GuiIngame.renderGameOverlay. With no one listening, the game's own runs as usual.
# Where the connection goes out (engine/Net, for a mod that talks through a proxy): in NetworkManager.createNetworkManagerAndConnect,
# the channel initializer and the destination address go through whoever is listening. Scoped to that single function: the server
# list ping and the rest of the game do not change. With no one registered, both go straight through.
# ... and the network thread group (LazyLoadBase.getValue, with no lock in the game) goes out through engine/Net.lazy, one thread at a
# time: the --server connection in startGame raced with the Loader creating the group and got null ("group").
# Client settings (engine/ClientSettings): GameSettings.sendSettingsToServer (avh.c) only sends the
# C15PacketClientSettings when something it carries changes or the connection is new — the volume screen saves the options on
# every frame while a control is dragged, and each time it sent the same packet (hundreds per second with the
# Stein FPS: a server with a packet limit disconnected). And options.txt is written there at most every 250 ms.
# Sound (engine/SoundGuard): reloadSoundSystem's unloadSoundSystem waits for the sound system that is still starting on the
# "Sound Library Loader" thread — a resource reload during startup (a mod that reloads twice in a row does this) skipped the
# shutdown and left two systems alive: duplicated or mistimed sound.
# HUD grid (Stein Loader): hotbar, health and hunger, experience, item name and chat, which the Loader draws wherever the player placed them.
# Click and mouse hover on the moved chat (GuiChat).
# Freeze watchdog (engine/Watchdog): counts what arrives from the server (Packet.processPacket inside
# NetworkManager.channelRead0), what goes out, and the game ticks. When the player is in a world and all of this stops, the
# watchdog dumps the threads to the log — it is the only way to see a bottlenecked thread. What goes out passes through two
# writeAndFlush calls: the one in dispatchPacket, when already on the network thread, and the one in the deferred Runnable (ek$4.run), through
# which almost everything goes — the game sends packets from the game thread. The first alone would give 9 packets in half a minute.
# RenderGlobal.renderEntities (bfr.a(Lpk;Lbia;F)V): each entity draw of the RenderManager — renderEntitySimple
# (biu.a) and the second pass renderMultipass (biu.b) — goes through the mods, which can refuse to let the entity be
# drawn. Body, armor, name and shadow disappear together; it is not the game's invisibility.
# Sprint that survives a hit (engine/Sprint, a mod option, off by default): the
# EntityPlayer.attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem drops sprinting right after the knockback
# (setSprinting(false), the 1.8 "sprint reset"). Only this call, and only inside the hit:
# outside it the game keeps toggling sprint as usual.
# Ghost ally (a mod hiding players): RendererLivingEntity.renderModel
# (bjl.a(Lpr;FFFFFF)V) already chooses between drawing normally, not drawing, and drawing at 15% without writing
# depth — the ghost the game makes of someone who is invisible and on your team. The two questions that
# lead to that choice go through the mods, and only inside that method: isInvisible() and
# isInvisibleToPlayer(player). That way the ghost is the game's own, with its code.
# The mod's ghost is fainter than the game's 15% (GameHooksEntity.ghostColor): the one color call in
# renderModel, GlStateManager.color(1, 1, 1, 0.15F), only on the translucent path.
# And the layers (armor, held item, cape) do not come out on the ghost: the game draws them outside
# invisibility — which is why an invisible player in armor becomes "walking armor" —, and a 15% silhouette
# with solid armor on top would show nothing of what is behind it.
# The ghost does not burn on screen (Render.doRenderShadowAndFire, biv.b(Lpk;DDDFF)V): the flames are drawn
# outside the model, like the armor, and a 15% silhouette inside a solid fire is the opposite of what the
# ghost does. It keeps burning for the server and everything else.
# And it does not emit potion particles (EntityLivingBase.updatePotionEffects, pr.bi()V): without the potion color the game
# emits none. The game already emits fewer for someone invisible — one in fifteen —, but "fewer" still marks
# The ghost does not flash red when taking damage (RendererLivingEntity.doRender, bjl.a(Lpr;DDDFF)V): the
# setDoRenderBrightness paints the whole model before drawing — red from the hit, white from the creeper, dark
# from death — and the game unpaints afterwards. Answering that nothing was painted leaves nothing to unpaint.
# Stein Loader 0.1.14: the end of the drawn world, plugin channel packet, sent chat and sound — the four that a Forge mod
# EntityRenderer.renderWorldPass (bfk.a(IFJ)V): after the only disableFog (bfl.n), the one that closes the translucent layer,
# before the upper clouds and the hand — the place of Forge's RenderWorldLastEvent.
# Bridge, which calls it and hands the channel and the bytes to the mods already on the game thread.
# Stein Sync in the server list (hooks/GameHooksServers): the Gson parse of the status JSON in
# S00PacketServerInfo.readPacketData (jr.a(Lem;)V) also reads the "steinSync" offer, kept on the ServerStatusResponse (js); the body of
# S00PacketServerInfo.processPacket (jr.a(Ljp;)V) copies it to the ServerData (bde) the pinger's handler is pinging; and
# after each IGuiListEntry.drawEntry of GuiListExtended.drawSlot (awd.a(IIIIII)V) the listeners draw over a server entry.
# Stein Sync login marker (hooks/GameHooksServers.connectPacket, stein-sync docs/protocol.md section 6): the
# NetworkManager.sendPacket (ek.a(Lff;)V) calls of GuiConnecting's connection thread (awz$1.run) go through the Bridge,
# which hands the login handshake's address to the Loader; without the Loader's listener the packet goes out as made.
# Stein Sync QUIC transport (engine/Net.loginConnect, stein-sync docs/protocol.md section 7): GuiConnecting's
# NetworkManager.createNetworkManagerAndConnect (ek.a(Ljava/net/InetAddress;IZ)Lek;) is marked as a join, so a listener
# of engine/Net can take a join over QUIC while server list pings (the same function, from OldServerPinger) stay TCP.
# A transport inside the JVM (Kwik's QUIC: a Netty LocalChannel to the Loader's link) carries a real server's compressed
# stream: NetworkManager.isLocalChannel (ek.c) where the client turns compression on (NetHandlerLoginClient's
# handleEnableCompression bcx.a(Lji;)V, NetHandlerPlayClient's handleSetCompressionLevel bcy.a(Lgl;)V) answers false
# for it (engine/Net.isLocalChannel); the integrated server's channel stays local.
# Stein Sync Tick's `applied` (net/SyncApplied, stein-sync docs/protocol.md section 5.5): each task
# PacketThreadUtil.checkThreadAndEnqueue (fh.a) hands to the game thread (IThreadListener.addScheduledTask, od.a) is numbered with
# its packet, and the packet's processPacket (ff.a) in that task (fh$1.run) counts it as handled. The arrival count is in
# Stein Sync login refusal hint (hooks/GameHooksServers, protocol section 6.2): the reason of a login Disconnect
# (S00PacketDisconnect.readPacketData, jj.a(Lem;)V, PacketBuffer.readChatComponent em.d) is shown to the Loader, and the screen
# NetHandlerLoginClient.onDisconnect (bcx.a(Leu;)V) shows for it goes through the Loader, which may join again at once
# instead (a server that requires Stein, joined without the server list's offer).
# Stein Sync client messages (hooks/GameHooksSync, the Loader's SteinSyncClient; stein-sync docs/protocol.md section 5): the
# packets EntityPlayerSP.onUpdate (bew.t_) and onUpdateWalkingPlayer (bew.p) send through NetHandlerPlayClient.addToSendQueue
# (bcy.a(Lff;)V), and the end of onUpdateWalkingPlayer; the attack PlayerControllerMP.attackEntity (bda.a(Lwn;Lpk;)V) sends;
# the C07/C08 of clickBlock (bda.b(Lcj;Lcq;)Z), onPlayerDamageBlock (bda.c(Lcj;Lcq;)Z), resetBlockRemoving (bda.c()V) and
# (bcy.a(Lfv;)V) and handleMultiBlockChange (bcy.a(Lfz;)V). Without a Stein Sync connection each one does what the game does.
# Stein Sync move (engine/SyncMove, stein-sync docs/protocol.md 5.5 and physics-spec.md 15.6, 15.7, 18): while the Loader says a
# Stein Sync proxy runs the player's movement, the client collides with the blocks the proxy's physics uses; otherwise each hook
# does what the game does. In World.getCollidingBoundingBoxes (adm.a(Lpk;Laug;)Ljava/util/List;) each Block.addCollisionBoxesToList
# (afh.a) goes through it: a chest or anvil adds the box of its own state, never the kind's shared bounds (drawing, outline and
# crosshair keep those). The World.getBlockState (adm.p) of the movement code reads a column the extended distance keeps (the server
# dropped it) as air: the collision gathering, Entity.moveEntity (pk.d), doBlockCollisions (pk.Q), EntityLivingBase's
# (bew.e(Lcj;)Z); and Chunk.isLoaded (amy.o) in moveEntityWithHeading, the gravity of a column not received, answers false for it.
# Stein Sync reconciliation (engine/SyncReplay, stein-sync docs/protocol.md milestone 7): while the Loader says a Stein Sync
# proxy holds the authority over the player's movement, each tick's input and state are kept, and a Correction restores a tick and
# runs the ticks after it again with the game's own movement code. Off (no such connection) each hook does what the game does.
# Before World.isBlockLoaded (adm.e) at the start of EntityPlayerSP.onUpdate (bew.t_): the changes since the last tick (teleport,
# velocity, hits). MovementInput.updatePlayerMoveState (beu.a) and KeyBinding.isKeyDown (avb.d, the sprint key) in
# EntityPlayerSP.onLivingUpdate (bew.m): the tick's input is noted, or given back in a replay. In a replay the player's sounds
# (World.playSound, adm.a, in EntityPlayerSP.playSound, bew.a(Ljava/lang/String;FF)V) and the splash particles
# (World.spawnParticle, adm.a, in Entity.resetHeight, pk.X) are dropped. Entity.setVelocity (pk.i) in
# NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityVelocity (bcy.a(Lhm;)V): the server's velocity for the player is noted as a value set.
# GuiScreen.sendChatMessage(String, boolean) (axu.b): EntityPlayerSP.sendChatMessage (bew.e) goes through the mods — chat
# and command, before going to the server (Forge's ClientChatEvent; client-only commands).
# SoundHandler.playSound (bpz.a(Lbpj;)V): SoundManager.playSound (bpx.c) goes through the mods — swap or silence the sound
# Virtual container (an auto-refill feature of a mod): the chest the server opens can become just the container, with no screen
# 1.7 animations (engine/OldAnimations, Lens option; visual only). First person, in
# ItemRenderer.renderItemInFirstPerson (bfn.a(F)V): the frame's swing (getSwingProgress) is kept and goes to
# transformFirstPersonItem (bfn.b, private) along with the item in use (the swing while blocking); and the held item's renderItem
# marks the 1.7 position for the model transform.
# ... the sword blocking in third person (the renderItem of LayerHeldItem.doRenderLayer) ...
# ... and, in RenderItem.renderItemModelTransform, the model's applyTransform: for the marked item, the 1.7 calculation applies.
# ModelBiped.render (bbj.a(Lpk;FFFFFF)V): setRotationAngles (virtual, ModelPlayer's too) is fixed afterwards —
# the blocking arm without the 1.8 y rotation, on the player and on the armor.
# RendererLivingEntity.renderLayers: each layer's shouldCombineTextures — the armor layer accepts the damage color.
# Minecraft.sendClickBlockToController (ave.b(Z)V): the isUsingItem that makes it return without mining; while using an item with attack
# held on a block, the hand swings on screen only (no mining and no packet).
# Physics trace (diag/PhysicsTrace, only with -Dsteinbridge.diag.physicsTrace): the player's state right before and right
# after each runTick (s) of runGameLoop (av), for Stein Sync's clean-room physics replay.
# The trace's attack and block-action records (same class; each call goes on to the game's own method, the record is
# written only with the property): EntityPlayer.attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem (wn.f) in PlayerControllerMP.attackEntity
# (bda.a), and World.addBlockEvent (on WorldClient, bdb.c) in NetHandlerPlayClient.handleBlockAction (bcy.a(Lfu;)V).
# The benchmark's CPU zones: the end of each zone, after every other rule of the same call (the begins are at the top
